concept.name: Poison Message Handling

relationships.description: Connects Poison Message Handling to caching in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Isolating unprocessable queue or stream messages with bounded retries and Dead-Letter Queues so one bad payload never stalls a partition.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of poison message handling—from why infinite retries cause Kafka rebalance storms to non-blocking retry topics and DLQ redrive guards.

spark.summary: Poison message handling isolates unprocessable queue or stream messages—caused by malformed payloads, schema drift, or deterministic business-rule bugs—so they do not loop infinitely and starve healthy traffic.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never let a single bad message block a partition or burn 100% of consumer CPU; bound retries with exponential backoff, then quarantine to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) with full error context.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **poison message** (or poison pill) is any event or job that a consumer repeatedly fails to process due to a **deterministic fault**—malformed JSON, unexpected Avro/Protobuf schema, missing foreign key, or an unhandled edge case—rather than a transient outage.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Transient Retry vs. Deterministic DLQ Quarantine (CONSUME -> RETRY TOPIC -> DLQ QUARANTINE); ErrorHandlingDeserializer -> Retry Topic -> Audited DLQ (orders.created -> Order Consumer -> orders.retry.1m -> orders.dlq).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance strict per-key ordering against partition throughput and prevention at the producer. A 12-partition `orders.created` consumer uses `ErrorHandlingDeserializer`, routes `TransientError` to `orders.retry.1m` (capped at 3 attempts), fast-fails `ValidationError` to.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore Kafka poison pills, consumer rebalance storms, and Dead-Letter Queue patterns.

learningJourney.title: What is a Poison Message
learningJourney.explanation:
A **poison message** (or poison pill) is any event or job that a consumer repeatedly fails to process due to a **deterministic fault**—malformed JSON, unexpected Avro/Protobuf schema, missing foreign key, or an unhandled edge case—rather than a transient outage.

Because at-least-once brokers (Kafka, SQS, RabbitMQ) redeliver unacknowledged messages, an unguarded poison message loops forever: stalling its Kafka partition or pinning SQS workers at 100% CPU.

sectionDiagram.title: Transient Retry vs. Deterministic DLQ Quarantine
sectionDiagram.summary: Fast-failing schema/parse errors straight to the DLQ keeps partitions moving while transient faults get bounded retries.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how a Poison Message works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Poison Message Handling (Rebalance Storms)
learningJourney.explanation: A single 2 KB poison pill can trigger a cluster-wide outage in two ways: (1) in Kafka, blocking retries (`Thread.sleep`) exceeding `max.poll.interval.ms` (default 5 min) trigger a **consumer group rebalance** that hands the exact same poison pill to the next consumer in a death spiral; (2) if `JsonDeserializer` throws *before* your listener `try/catch`, the consumer crashes and restarts forever.

ideas.title: Wrap Deserializers with ErrorHandlingDeserializer
ideas.description: Catch malformed bytes inside the deserializer itself and forward the raw payload + exception headers to the DLQ.

ideas.title: Truncate Stack Traces in DLQ Headers
ideas.description: Appending full stack traces on every retry can breach SQS's 256 KB or Kafka's 1 MB limit—store a 1 KB summary in headers and log the full trace by `trace_id`.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Poison Message Handling under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Poison Message Handling is critical (and where to skip)
learningJourney.explanation: Quarantine poison pills on all durable business queues and ordered streams; skip DLQ replay overhead only for loss-tolerant telemetry.

benefits: Non-blocking retry topics + DLQ unblock healthy keys on the same partition immediately.
costs: Subsequent valid events for the *same* entity key may process out-of-order while the earlier event sits in the DLQ.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Shared Work Queues (SQS / RabbitMQ)
benefits: Native `RedrivePolicy` (`maxReceiveCount = 3`) moves failing jobs to a DLQ with zero custom broker code.
costs: Requires `dlq_depth > 0` alerting and a tested replay runbook so the DLQ does not become a data graveyard.

benefits: Drop and count malformed 0.001% metric samples instead of operating a DLQ replay pipeline.
costs: Not acceptable for financial, order, or audit events.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How Exception Classification & Bounded Retries are implemented
learningJourney.explanation: Disable `enable.auto.commit` in Kafka, classify exceptions explicitly into retryable vs. non-retryable, preserve diagnostic metadata (`exception_class`, `topic`, `partition`, `offset`, `dlq-replay-count`), and cap automated DLQ redrives to avoid ping-pong loops.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Blocking Backoff vs. Non-Blocking Retry Topics vs. Schema Registry
learningJourney.explanation: Balance strict per-key ordering against partition throughput and prevention at the producer.

benefits: Keeps main partition consumers unblocked and never exceeds `max.poll.interval.ms`.
costs: Can reorder events for the same entity key while one event is delayed in a retry topic.

benefits: Preserves strict per-key partition ordering for short 100–2,000 ms blips.
costs: Stalls all other keys sharing that partition if a downstream outage lasts minutes.

benefits: Prevents schema-drift poison pills at CI/producer serialization before they ever enter Kafka.
costs: Does not prevent business-logic edge cases (e.g., missing foreign keys).

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production example: Multi-Tier Kafka Retry & Audited DLQ Redrive
learningJourney.explanation: A 12-partition `orders.created` consumer uses `ErrorHandlingDeserializer`, routes `TransientError` to `orders.retry.1m` (capped at 3 attempts), fast-fails `ValidationError` to `orders.dlq` with truncated headers, and alerts on `dlq_depth > 0`. After a consumer fix deploys, an audited redrive job stamps `dlq-replay-count: 1`.

sectionDiagram.title: ErrorHandlingDeserializer -> Retry Topic -> Audited DLQ
sectionDiagram.summary: Both malformed payloads and transient faults commit off the main partition immediately so healthy traffic never stalls.

knowledgeCheck.question: A Kafka consumer sleeps synchronously for 6 minutes retrying a poison message while `max.poll.interval.ms` is set to 5 minutes. What happens?

options.text: The broker evicts the consumer and triggers a group rebalance, handing the exact same poison pill to another consumer in an endless storm
options.feedback: Correct: blocking the poll loop past `max.poll.interval.ms` triggers rebalance storms across the consumer group.

options.text: Kafka automatically moves the message to a `.dlq` topic after 5 minutes
options.feedback: Kafka has no built-in broker-side DLQ; consumers must route failed messages explicitly.

options.text: The offset is auto-committed and the message is dropped
options.feedback: The consumer is evicted before committing, causing redelivery to peers.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
